[Click here if you're a maintainer who wants to add another changeset to this PR](https://github.com/jrmajor/svelte/new/bind-this-warning-2?filename=.changeset/neat-yaks-serve.md&value=---%0A%22svelte%22%3A%20patch%0A---%0A%0Afix%3A%20false%20positive%20%60non_reactive_update%60%20when%20using%20%60bind%3Athis%60%20(simpler%20alternative)%0A)

Thank you, but we'd like to keep this as is. Closing because we want to keep the warning in case it's inside an if block. With this PR, you'd get false negatives (which are worse than a few false positives). The amount of additional analysis we would need to avoid false positives in edge cases is not worth it.

A simple drop down use case triggers this warning for me:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
let dropdownComp: ComponentExports<typeof Dropdown>;
</script>

<Dropdown bind:this={dropdownComp}>
    <DropdownCustomButton onclick={dropdownComp.toggleOpen}>Button</DropdownCustomButton>
    <!-- omitted -->
</Dropdown>
```

(note: am using a ComponentExports helper per https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/pull/13441)

And currently the VS Code extension whacks a HTML comment based ignore statement below the script tag (meaning zero impact) when I ask it to ignore the warning for that ```let dropdownComp``` line.

```svelte
<!-- svelte-ignore non_reactive_update -->
<Dropdown bind:this={dropdownComp}>
    <DropdownCustomButton onclick={dropdownComp.toggleOpen}>Button</DropdownCustomButton>
    <!-- omitted -->
</Dropdown>
```

I'm on all the latest bumps (I believe) of Svelte 5.

I am not yet knowledgable (update - see below) on how to correctly ignore a svelte check error on a single line similar to how one can do with @eslint-ignore and would accept that at this point (I do something similar to keep prefer-const on when using $bindable).

Sharing as it led me to believe I should be using state for bound vars for a fair while, and now I'm less ignorant I'm looking to turn the check off altogether if I can't find the one-line version. Perhaps consider these impacts in addition to the false-negative/false-positive trade off.

---

Update: I've got the ignore working, I had to add an eslint disable, unsure if that's useful or just bad eslint config on my part. The general risk of misguiding noobs is still worthy of stating IMO and maybe can feed into other late tooling improvements.

```typescript
// eslint-disable-next-line svelte/no-unused-svelte-ignore
// svelte-ignore non_reactive_update
let dropdownComp1: ComponentExports<typeof Dropdown>; 
```

---

Another update (sorry but HTH!):

Was wondering why it was intermittent and compared my cases. When I use a function to call the bound var the warning goes away. It's only when I just pass the function in as a direct property.

So this results in no-warning:
```svelte
<DropdownCustomButton
    onclick={() => {
        dropdownComp.toggleOpen();
    }}>Button</DropdownCustomButton
>
```

But do this and the warning is shown:
```svelte
<DropdownCustomButton onclick={dropdownComp.toggleOpen}>Button</DropdownCustomButton>
```

issue_context.title: False positive “updated, but not declared with `$state`” warning
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

With the following code in runes mode:

```svelte
<script>
	let input;
</script>

{#if true}
	<input bind:this={input}/>
	<button onclick={() => input?.focus()}>focus input</button>
{/if}
```

I get the following warning: `input is updated, but is not declared with $state(...). Changing its value will not correctly trigger updates (non_reactive_update)`.

This doesn't happen unless the bound element is defined in a conditional.

### Reproduction

Here's above example in [REPL](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAAE0WNTQ7CIBCFr0LGTZs0do-0xnOIC0shTmwHUgYTQ7i7KV24e_PN-8ngcLER5D0DPVcLEm4hQAf8DfsRP3ZhCx1EnzazE3Ug6QOjpyi2RDb2oyZNKpoNA--aF8sCKSS-aFL9_0H5hE7wlmzZbap6xIQ0S35hHHIFpRaymhKzJ-HJLGjeQ25aMYxH7_XsvEmxactYxUFVf0RGTblHVzRBB6uf0aGdQdbdR_kBxu8KY_YAAAA=).

### Logs

_No response_

### System Info

```shell
System:
  OS: macOS 14.6.1
  CPU: (12) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-9750H CPU @ 2.60GHz

```


### Severity

annoyance

That is not a false positive, at least in the general case. The compiler cannot in all cases determine that the conditional is always true (if it could there would not be much reason to have it there anyway). If the condition changes, the value of the variable bound to the element also changes. If it is lacking `$state`, there will be no updates, e.g.: ```svelte

typeof input: {typeof input}

{#if show} {/if} ``` [REPL](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAACk2OzW7EIAyEXwW5PSTSqrmzkKrPUXpICChoswYF0x8h3r0CWrU3f2OPZzJYd5gI_DUDLncDHF5CgAvQV6gQ381BBi4QfTp1VUSXuA_kPEZ2JjRxmhUqFFGfLlCd6TDEHIZE11-Ku_9gkj1GWsgMdjmiGa8KxfTnQhHmGuxt93KW_2MRU5gVigasbqQCvRt9W_2nArY63Hhjs8lc8wrrzfKDs61AqW1-HrRz2l2Uub9vtyTWROSRedSH0zeZh5HJuTd4frJepziMZW5DV8XULbPCPDlbFMIF7n5z1pkNOJ3JlLfyDZUDDo9rAQAA) ~~There seems to be a different issue, though. If `$state` is used, the value is not cleared on unmount ([REPL](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAACk2OzW7EIAyEXwW5PSTSqrlToOpzlB4SAgrarEHB9EeId68IrbY3z4w9_go4v9sE_K0AzjcLHF5jhAvQd2wifdidLFwghXyY5ohu8RDJB0zsyGjTpDRqFMkcPlKbabfEPMZMTLLHRDPZYXz-C9IWPu--m_dkWyimewGKqBpDcL2Gs_JfVjFFpVH0Fy2RGsxmzXUJXxrY4nHlp7arLO1fZR2yPHh3AtRG81twrtPmkyy9_twlsWSigCyg2b25yjKMTKpO8PLkgslpGKs6h-6KqZ8ojWXyrmqEC9zC6p23K3A6sq3v9QfiZOYUdgEAAA==)).~~ (It's just `null` and `null` also has the `typeof` value of `object`.)

There is no point in assigning a variable if it is never read, e.g. `input?.focus()` reads `input`.

The warning could probably only be omitted if the compiler can determine that a read is guaranteed to be outside of an effect (which is almost never the case I think).

> The warning could probably only be omitted if the compiler can determine that a read is guaranteed to be outside of an effect

Yes, that's what this issue is about.

> (which is almost never the case I think).

It is almost always the case with `bind:this`. The example in Svelte docs also doesn't reference the bound variable in a reactive context: https://svelte.dev/docs/element-directives#bind-this.

Also, the compiler already analyzes whether a variable is read in a reactive context. It just doesn't work with `bind:this`, because compiler assumes it's bidirectional like other bindings (e.g. `bind:value`). Here's an [example](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAAE0WOwW6DQAxEf8X1KVVA9EwXpHxHyYEspl11sVdrb6MI8e8VoVJv9pvxjFecQyTF9mNFHhfCFi8pYYX2SPuiPxSNsEKVkv1O3IFaSRaEFXJh0qYfeGCnPodk-2yRDLwUNujg7X1g1_yL7F7qGuyL4D5mDvwJk5ACi8GYEo0ZCkdShYcUKOxlWYjteZBppkzsCW4U5Q513f_Frc-27SADu1sxEwZhH4P_7tbTK3T98dL5vPVGaq45TD1WuMgU5kATtpYLbdftF6I4Rl4aAQAA).

> Also, the compiler already analyzes whether a variable is read in a reactive context.

Well, it tries [and apparently fails](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAACmWQ3WqEMBBGX2UIpausaK9dFfoctRdrdrJkN85IMukP4ruXaOkKvUpy-JjM-WZlrMOg6rdZ0XlEVavXaVKFku8pPcIHOkFVqMDR60SaDdU8iWUK4CNhqLqeemqC9naSdBc7TuwFZnB8hQWM5xEOZRUkGlNuI8pbOJxS1qGA5kgCLbxshK9ZlkPbbTw_QVXB4PmOBM9ADJ9nT5auPTXV41NqhijCBEzaWX1v592M43HpBIM01RbqelKFGvlijcWLqsVHXIq_FvaLPuq4hX0V-LU6mkg6dZFUMz3kMCeFJzQGtfxqrKgXzRTYYbklszxfbZd0LP-3eV9-AHZcNOKfAQAA).

As I said, in most cases it should not be possible to statically determine that something is *not* in an `$effect`.
Of course usage in the template guarantees usage in an effect but the other way around is much less obvious.

> Well, it tries and apparently fails.

It does that analysis only for templates:
https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/blob/2d03dc55c66c7d540be12096898ef3d47f4a8464/packages/svelte/src/compiler/phases/2-analyze/index.js#L570

> As I said, in most cases it should not be possible to statically determine that something is not in an $effect.
> Of course usage in the template guarantees usage in an effect but the other way around is much less obvious.

Probably that's the reason why it doesn't attempt to do that elsewhere. But this issue is about false positive, not unanalyzed false negatives, so this seems out of scope.

> There seems to be a different issue, though. If `$state` is used, the value is not cleared on unmount 

It sees the value to `null` which is correctly happening. Maybe because you're using `typeof` and that is an object on `null` too?

> > There seems to be a different issue, though. If `$state` is used, the value is not cleared on unmount
> 
> It sees the value to `null` which is correctly happening. Maybe because you're using `typeof` and that is an object on `null` too?

You are correct, it becomes null which technically is an object, so that works as intended.

---

> But this issue is about false positive, not unanalyzed false negatives, so this seems out of scope.

My point is: By trying to get rid of warnings like this, you are likely to introduce false negatives.
It's changing, just use `$state`.

I'm a little confused with this issue. We are warning you because you're referencing a variable that isn't state inside a block. Regardless of the fact the block is unconditional – you're still opening up the `bind:this` to be dynamic and thus should be state, otherwise it won't properly update if the block changes.

I think using his test in the deployed repl shows what he's trying to say

[REPL](https://svelte-5-preview-qbysiakog-svelte.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAAA42PUUvEMBCE_0pYfWjhsNi-9dqCv8OK3DUbDeZ2S7MtSOh_l1jPK_UUH_djZnYmgLEOPZSPAehwQijhoe9hB_Lex8NP6ARhB57HoYuk8t1ge2laasWhKOJnQtT3-w3II_hCmtFvVN8o_4kKVatbLwfBJN23VGWXlxRiMTaryPkKzK_BYo4BlbaTOlrSpbxaX4dVUFNl2k7LmxtrlAwjRo9sPefNK8dvmvwvzarvf1TFRRUya5Y5x1GESTF1znZvdUhSVTeqY_Ls8M7xS3Juks6NYa6yxdG0BDs4sbbGoobyc-zT_AFC2aYzEQIAAA==)

As long as you are never reading the variable from the template there's no need for it to be state because the variable is still updated so if you read it from an event listener it will be the right one.

This also uncover another problem which is that if you access the variable in an effect instead of the template the warning doesn't fire (this also happens today tho)

> you're still opening up the bind:this to be dynamic and thus should be state, otherwise it won't properly update if the block changes.

It _will_ update properly — you can see that in [this REPL](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAAE0WQMW-EMAyF_4qVdgDpdOwUkDp06dAO7VI1HSA4EF2wUWJ6PSH-ewXctVPynuxnf56VdR6jyj9nRfWAKleP46gOSi7jKuI3ekF1UJGnYFan2K2cR3FMEcJEGLNKk6YimuBGWf_iUcDROMnDTcWez1DCfZRaMLG1j5g-aCqy_y56567zCNIjmB7NqeEfqKkF4505bXYziTBBDRbPIG7AeCyaUGn64AlMTRARwREYpshbVH1dBAyHgEb8BUxfU4cRbOABnjwOSALCQJP31zhNf-_evR6k1Oq2llbQOGrzTWNbziveAvsh5jtnN95lhb8GbOXSu1jOm7GstXPm7LJP28GYNtZyTlIoqxvG0XOXPL-9vhyjBEeds5dkC0nTpfLc7YRFtodUmtRBDdw667BVuYQJl6_lFzT0zI_sAQAA). Svelte assigns to this variable regardless of whether it's `$state()`. The warning is needed only when you read this variable in template. In this case, it's only referenced in closure, so Svelte shouldn't care.

@jrmajor It won't update properly. Try putting the variable in an `$effect` or `$effect.pre` and then compare it to `$state`. Nor is it reactive as a prop – it's basically useless and definitely not reactive.

[Here are the example](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAAE41SwYrbMBD9lUENJIFgQ4_e2FCWvfTQHtpLqXtwlLEtVp4R0rjbYPzvRZY32e3S0oOx51nvzbzRm1RrLAZVfJ8UNQOqQn1wTh2UXFwswk-0guqgAo9eR-SYoIKdGKYAfiQMeVVTTcegvXESv8UMjr3APQ-OCUneQ-t5gG2W36AsSW3vIiE-FgUMuVHunqvQ8xOUsAnSCO7axgbcx59UywbbFrVkzuNut4eygmnREc0U2GJmudstavuIz_tXtP-lHPObKfrKXWcRpEfQPerHE_-Chs6grdGPC3waRZiggRafQMyAITuefFXTNx5BNwQBEQzB2hCkb1bLoNl71GIvoPuGOgxpYw8WByQBYaDR2lWupus7seN9lbV6HqtWcDJ0LpYaz-UUFzlDuqfpnWmXzc7R5SqwHJfehHJagDmenXLTzqlbMsa0eC2ntL6Xe_v45fOnLIg31Jn2sq5xP1eWu-TwmCeRNPaLZKwNIa_UQQ18Nq3BsyrEjzgfrrm8Ef4dz1sG43RyVS9h4zy7sPsjQH9Pwjae3x7S9AvrdSTeTvtj_g2y5HzFUQMAAA==)

> @jrmajor It won't update properly. Try putting the variable in an `$effect` or `$effect.pre` and then compare it to `$state`. [See here](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAAE42QP0_EMAzFv4oVGK7S6W4vbSUGFgYYYEGEoZc6bURqV4kLnKp-d5S2_NuYEr_Ez36_SVnnMar8eVJU96hydT0Maq_kPKQivqEXVHsVeQwmKcUq5TyIY4oQRsJ4rDRpKqIJbpB0F48CjoZRrr6q2PE7lHAZpRbc2dpHzNIjablEa9HIYQi422VQVjAlWYthiuzx4LndLW5Z0ufsT9t_W4rjz370yG3rEaRDMB2a1xN_QE0NGO_M6yKfRhEmqMHiO4jrMR6KU6g0PfEIpiaIiOAItoEgXb1FBsMhoBF_BtPV1GIEG7iHG489koAw0Oj9Zqfp-1y7E_pSq6-1tIKToyZfamzKKYGcYUU-XTi7kJ1Tys1g-S6di-W0CHP6Ox2dnddpazCmJWs5rfh-c7t9uL87RAmOWmfPG8Zsrjy3a8LiuJpUmtRe9dw467BRuYQR55f5Eyxi7MNWAgAA).

Yeah if you read it in an effect it will not update but if you never read it from an effect and only use it in events for example it will work fine so the warning is not needed. But i think we should also add the logic to see if it's used in an effect and warn if that's the case (obviously you can't always know for sure if behind a function there's an effect but it's a starter)

> > @jrmajor It won't update properly. Try putting the variable in an `$effect` or `$effect.pre` and then compare it to `$state`. [See here](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAAE42QP0_EMAzFv4oVGK7S6W4vbSUGFgYYYEGEoZc6bURqV4kLnKp-d5S2_NuYEr_Ez36_SVnnMar8eVJU96hydT0Maq_kPKQivqEXVHsVeQwmKcUq5TyIY4oQRsJ4rDRpKqIJbpB0F48CjoZRrr6q2PE7lHAZpRbc2dpHzNIjablEa9HIYQi422VQVjAlWYthiuzx4LndLW5Z0ufsT9t_W4rjz370yG3rEaRDMB2a1xN_QE0NGO_M6yKfRhEmqMHiO4jrMR6KU6g0PfEIpiaIiOAItoEgXb1FBsMhoBF_BtPV1GIEG7iHG489koAw0Oj9Zqfp-1y7E_pSq6-1tIKToyZfamzKKYGcYUU-XTi7kJ1Tys1g-S6di-W0CHP6Ox2dnddpazCmJWs5rfh-c7t9uL87RAmOWmfPG8Zsrjy3a8LiuJpUmtRe9dw467BRuYQR55f5Eyxi7MNWAgAA).
> 
> Yeah if you read it in an effect it will not update but if you never read it from an effect and only use it in events for example it will work fine so the warning is not needed. But i think we should also add the logic to see if it's used in an effect and warn if that's the case (obviously you can't always know for sure if behind a function there's an effect but it's a starter)

It doesn't work as a prop either. We can't add logic to see if it's used in an effect as we don't know if it will be used – it could be passed around to a function that then uses it. Our best bet it is to warn if it's used anywhere but a `bind:this`.

Honestly, I'm of the position that we should just disallow `let thing` entirely and enforce that it's always declared with `$state` otherwise you can't bind to it.

The analysis that emit's this warning is only for template, it doesn't analyze effects.

And I know that template is also an effect, but the whole point is that this variable is *not* read there, only written.

> The analysis that emit's this warning is only for template, it doesn't analyze effects.
> 
> And I know that template is also an effect, but the whole point is that this variable is _not_ read there, only written.

If it's not read anywhere, then we should just remove the binding altogether as it's completely not needed and thus overhead. If it is read somewhere, then it matters _where_ it is read – and if it's referenced anywhere but the `bind:this` then it _must_ be `$state` IMO as there are far too many gotchas coming around from this now. Really, it's just backwards that we allow you to bind a variable that isn't `$state` to a variable in runes mode and expect people to navigate around the gotchas – it should _always_ be `$state` or it won't work IMO.

> Honestly, I'm of the position that we should just disallow let thing entirely and enforce that it's always declared with $state otherwise you can't bind to it.

Yeah that could be good too...is not that big of a deal and it will help the user in case of refactoring

> Nor is it reactive as a prop

Using it as a prop would still throw a warning after my fix, as it is a reference in the template.

> it's basically useless and definitely not reactive.

It's not useless — all I want to do is to `.focus()` it in some callback. It's exactly what I need. It's like saying that constants in JS are basically useless because you cannot reassign to them. Yeah, I don't want to and I don't need to, that's why I used `const`. If I try to reassign it, then TS yells at me. I would expect the same from Svelte — if I don't use `$state`, it means that I don't want something to be reactive. If I use it in reactive context anyway, then you can give me a warning.

> it should _always_ be `$state` or it won't work IMO.

> and it will help the user in case of refactoring

That makes sense for bidirectional bindings (like `bind:value`), but not for `bind:this` IMO. I've already used `bind:this` in a few projects dozen of times with Svelte 5 and non of these cases needed the value to be `$state`.

If you want to prevent gotchas and help users with upgrading, then covering `$effect` by the same analysis that happens for templates, like suggested by @brunnerh, would be a good idea, and I think would cover gotchas you're referring to without false positives.

> And I know that template is also an effect, but the whole point is that this variable is _not_ read there, only written.

It is read there. The compiled output is literally this:

```js
$.bind_this(input_1, ($$value) => input = $$value, () => input);
```

Notice that we read from it as the third argument? This warning is not a lie, it's a legit warning that will stop breakages. I really don't know why you're trying so hard to avoid using `$state` where it genuinely is needed.

> If you want to prevent gotchas and help users with upgrading, then covering `$effect` by the same analysis that happens for templates, like suggested by @brunnerh, would be a good idea, and I think would cover gotchas you're referring to without false positives.

We have a migration script that will help the majority of users with that. From my perspective, so many things can possibly go wrong with people assuming a simple `let something` works, when it quickly breaks down to not work. In one sense you say it's not reactive – but the very definition of reactive in Svelte 5 is that something either needs to be `$state` or `$derived`. This is consistent and helps people learn. If you suddenly say that a variable binding can be mutated by the framework (thus is reactive by definition) yet not need those properties adds to cognitive overload. We definitely don't want that – and the compiler can be smart enough to remove the need for a signal at the end of the day.

> Notice that we read from it as the third argument?

Looking at the implementation of `bind_this`, I don't think this callback is executed in `render_effect` (or it is, but in `untrack`), but your understanding of Svelte internals is definitely better than mine.

> I really don't know why you're trying so hard to avoid using `$state` where it genuinely is needed.

That's the first time in this discussion that somebody actually said that it _is_ read in effect (although I still don't think it is). I feel like everyone is trying to convince me that my example is broken, while it works perfectly fine. What do I need the `$state` for (except for not-confusing newcomers)?

> We have a migration script that will help the majority of users with that.

FYI, even with my fix, the migration script would still add `$state` in such cases.

> variable binding can be mutated by the framework (thus is reactive by definition)

Sorry, my understanding was that reactive variables are the ones that trigger effects.

> adds to cognitive overload. We definitely don't want that

I think it's as simple as it gets — if you don't use `$state`, then you don't trigger effects. Feel free to close this issue if you decide it's too hard for newcomers.

> I think it's as simple as it gets — if you don't use `$state`, then you don't trigger effects. Feel free to close this issue if you decide it's too hard for newcomers.

It's not about effects, but rather about being a signal. If you look at the compiled output when using a simple `let` we don't compile it to a signal `$.source`. But there in lies the complication, because you didn't use state, it can never be a signal. The inverse is that if you make it state and the compiler sees you never use it in an event handler or effect, then it can remove the need for a signal.

I'll defer to @dummdidumm and @Rich-Harris on this one, but this topic has come up time and time again – and I feel like we should make the usage consistent with other possibly-reactive use-cases. For example, try using `$state` and never mutating it and see the compiled output.

> but this topic has come up time and time again

Where has this topic come up previously? It came up repeatedly that people said "why does Svelte say my `bind:this` variable needs to be `$state` here, it clearly doesn't", and then we changed it so that it does not warn in this case. Since then, I haven't seen any occurence of "why is this warning (not) coming up for `bind:this`" threads except this one.

Given that it only came up now, and given that I still think the 90% case is well-solved with this (these are hints after all that should help you detect common mistakes, not strict errors or annoying warnings), I think we should just leave it as is and close this issue.

> > but this topic has come up time and time again
> 
> Where has this topic come up previously? It came up repeatedly that people said "why does Svelte say my `bind:this` variable needs to be `$state` here, it clearly doesn't", and then we changed it so that it does not warn in this case.
